You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm/boot/dts/at91-sama5d2_icp.dts`**
   - Removed the line `regulator-always-on;` from the `VDD_OTHER` regulator configuration. This change indicates that the VDD_OTHER regulator will no longer be kept enabled at all times.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in the device tree source file (`at91-sama5d2_icp.dts`) directly addresses a previously established configuration where the VDD_OTHER regulator was set to always be on. The removal of the `regulator-always-on;` line reflects a correction based on the observation that VDD_OTHER is not connected to any onboard consumer, thus it does not need to be continuously enabled. This change is part of a bug fix related to the earlier commit identified by the hash `68a95ef72cef`.

1. analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 
2. output the file name that is most likely to cause the bug.

You must include one or more code statements in point 1 and 2.
Code statements included in point 1 should be as brief as possible, only include the ones that are most related to the root cause and  the number of code statements may not exceed 3.


Here is the commit message:
ARM: dts: at91: sama5d2_icp: don't keep vdd_other enabled all
 the time

VDD_OTHER is not connected to any on board consumer thus it is not
needed to keep it enabled all the time.

Fixes: 68a95ef72cef ("ARM: dts: at91: sama5d2-icp: add SAMA5D2-ICP")
Signed-off-by: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220826083927.3107272-9-claudiu.beznea@microchip.com

Here is the root cause:
The VDD_OTHER regulator was incorrectly configured to be always enabled (`regulator-always-on;`), despite not being connected to any onboard consumer, leading to unnecessary power consumption and potential system inefficiencies.

Here is the patch:
 					regulator-initial-mode = <2>;
 					regulator-allowed-modes = <2>, <4>;
-					regulator-always-on;


The `regulator-always-on;` statement incorrectly configures the VDD_OTHER regulator to remain enabled at all times, despite it not being connected to any onboard consumer. This results in unnecessary power consumption and potential inefficiencies in the system.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c

```
Reason:
By removing the `regulator-always-on;` statement, the VDD_OTHER regulator is no longer forced to stay enabled continuously, thus preventing unnecessary power usage and improving overall system efficiency.
